newsitem.title: UK: TVA and EIB to swap mark and dollar bond proceeds.
newsitem.headline: TVA and EIB to swap mark and dollar bond proceeds.

text.p: The European Investment Bank and Tennessee Valley Authority will swap proceeds of two global bonds they are due to launch soon, syndicate managers said on Monday.
In a back-to-back swap rarely seen these days, the EIB will give the TVA the dollars from its planned bond, while the TVA will reciprocate with marks from its issue.
"The two deals will be swapped against each other, in an old-fashioned back-to-back swap," a syndicate head at a U.S. bank said.
Current practice is more usually for borrowers to do swaps through a counterparty rather than match needs exactly with another borrower.
In the EIB/TVA agreement, pay dates, coupon dates and maturity dates of both deals will stay the same.

TVA said earlier it would issue a 1.5 billion mark 10-year bond on Tuesday at a spread in the low- to mid-teens basis points over government bonds. Lead managers will be Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and Lehman Brothers.
The EIB will set a dollar global bond via CS First Boston and Lehman Brothers. A $1.0 billion 10-year deal in the high-teens b.p. over U.S. Treasuries was expected, dealers said.
Officials at Lehman Brothers, joint lead on both deals and said to be arranging the swap, were not immediately available for comment.
